reviews.author: Gregory Price
reviews.summary: The patch author posted an initial patch with a clear description of the problem and solution, but no feedback has been received yet.
reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, Sep 02, 2026 at 05:58:52PM -0400, Gregory Price wrote:
> find_next_best_node() picks the next-closest node for a fallback list
> from the full N_MEMORY set. Refactor it into find_next_best_node_in(),
> which takes an explicit candidates nodemask.
> 
> This enables building fallback lists with non-N_MEMORY candidates.
> 
> No functional change: every caller still selects from N_MEMORY.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Gregory Price <gourry@gourry.net>

Just realized this should carry an Ack from Balbir

Acked-by: Balbir Singh <balbirs@nvidia.com>

see - https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/62bf02dc-dab1-41bf-8204-eb3566628b93@nvidia.com/

reviews.author: Balbir Singh
reviews.summary: The reviewer acknowledged the patch and added an Acked-by tag, indicating they are in favor of the change.

2026-09-02.patch_summary: The patch refactors the find_next_best_node() function to find_next_best_node_in(), which takes an explicit candidates nodemask, enabling building fallback lists with non-N_MEMORY candidates without changing the callers' behavior.
